channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Oman Elevate Relations to Strategic Partnership Level
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited Oman, resulting in elevated relations to a strategic partnership. Discussions led to a joint project portfolio valued at $5 billion. Leaders agreed to adopt a roadmap and establish a Coordination Council to implement agreements, emphasizing mutual support within international frameworks.

item.title: Four Central Asian nations to launch unified electricity trading platform
item.description: Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Tajikistan are preparing to launch a unified electricity market. The 'Energia' Coordination and Dispatch Center is seeking a company to create and manage the trading platform. The project, supported by the World Bank, aims for transactions to begin by late 2028 or early 2029.

item.title: Turkish President Urges Muslim Nations to Increase Influence on Israel Regarding Gaza
item.description: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan has called on Muslim countries to intensify their efforts to influence Israel concerning the escalating humanitarian crisis in Gaza. He believes that joint action by Islamic states is necessary to resolve the situation in the region. Erdoğan highlighted the daily hardships faced by Gaza's residents and the obstacles to providing food supplies.

item.title: Kazakhstan Halts Illegal Diversion of Karatal River
item.description: Authorities in Kazakhstan's Zhetysu region have stopped an illegal attempt to change the course of the Karatal River. The Balhash-Alakol Basin Water Inspection, in collaboration with the regional environmental prosecutor's office, discovered that riverbed alteration work was conducted without proper authorization. Administrative measures have been taken against those responsible.

item.title: Kazakhstan Pursues Procedures for Launching Direct Flights to the USA
item.description: Kazakhstan is working towards launching its first direct flight to the United States by the end of 2027. Key steps include obtaining Category 1 status from the US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and acquiring new aircraft. Negotiations are ongoing, with preliminary audits showing positive results.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Improving Waste Management and Recycling Efficiency
item.description: Kazakhstan's Parliament discussed enhancing the waste management system and increasing recycling effectiveness. In 2025, an estimated 5 million tons of municipal solid waste were generated, with only 1.5 million tons recycled. Out of 2,911 landfills, just 577 meet environmental and sanitary requirements. Special attention was given to a landfill in the Atyrau region.

item.title: Kazakh Scientists Propose Monument for Kyrgyz Statesman Jusup Abdrakhmanov in Almaty or Astana
item.description: Kazakh scientists have proposed erecting a monument to Kyrgyz statesman Jusup Abdrakhmanov in either Almaty or Astana. The initiative was raised at a conference where Abdrakhmanov's contribution to saving hundreds of thousands during the 1932 famine was recognized. The proposal aims to honor his work and promote Kyrgyz-Kazakh friendship.

item.title: Kazakhstan: President Calls for Comprehensive Reform of Government System
item.description: Kazakhstan's President has emphasized the need for a fundamental reform of the government system, urging a review of the management structure from the government down to village akims. He also stressed the importance of utilizing digital technologies and artificial intelligence to enhance public service.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Progress on Health Sector Directives from People's Kurultai
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Health reports that 188 out of 250 directives issued during the People's Kurultai concerning the healthcare sector have been fulfilled or are in progress. This includes expanding access to high-tech medical care, opening catheterization labs, and equipping regional hospitals with CT scanners.

item.title: Central Asian glaciers may shrink by 60-80% by 2050 due to climate change
item.description: Glaciers in Central Asia could shrink by 60-80% by 2050 compared to 1950 levels, according to Kyrgyzstan's Deputy Minister of Natural Resources, Aysel Raimkulova. Temperatures in the region are rising nearly twice as fast as the global average, leading to significant economic damage from droughts and extreme weather.

item.title: Ancient Taraz Museum Unveils Rich Collection of Ceramic Artifacts and Jewelry
item.description: The State Historical and Cultural Museum-Reserve 'Ancient Taraz Monuments' holds numerous ancient artifacts, primarily from archaeological excavations between 2011 and 2017. Many items date back to the early and middle ages, including gold and silver jewelry discovered within ceramic pots, showcasing the advanced craftsmanship of ancient Taraz.

item.title: How Taliban Intelligence Controls Life in Afghan Districts
item.description: This report investigates the methods employed by Taliban intelligence to exert control over the lives of residents in various Afghan districts. It examines the extent of surveillance and the impact of these intelligence operations on daily life and local governance.

item.title: Do Taliban Forces Have Access to Turkish and Israeli Weapons?
item.description: This article explores the possibility of Taliban forces acquiring weapons of Turkish and Israeli origin. It investigates claims and assesses the potential implications of such access for regional security and the ongoing conflict dynamics in Afghanistan.

item.title: Kazakhstan and China to Open First Agricultural Research Center in Central Asia
item.description: Kazakhstan and China are set to launch the first joint agricultural research center in Central Asia. This initiative aims to foster scientific collaboration and advancements in the agricultural sector between the two nations.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Maternity Leave Payments for 2026 Explained
item.description: In 2026, Kazakhstan will calculate maternity leave payments based on a woman's average income over the last 12 months, with social contributions considered. Payments are a lump sum for 126 days, minus 10% pension contributions.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Overhaul Insurance Market by 2030
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to significantly reform its insurance market by 2030, aiming to expand services, improve accessibility, enhance payouts, and strengthen client protection. Key changes include mandatory housing insurance against natural disasters and new pension annuities.

item.title: DemirBank Supports Women's Entrepreneurship in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: DemirBank actively supports women's entrepreneurship in Kyrgyzstan by expanding access to finance and banking services. Collaborating with the IFC, the bank has allocated significant funds, with at least 25% designated for women-led businesses, and joined the Women Entrepreneurs Finance Code.

item.title: Chingiz Aitmatov Center Opens at Turan University in Almaty
item.description: A center and bust dedicated to renowned Kyrgyz writer Chingiz Aitmatov have been inaugurated at Turan University in Almaty. The new center aims to research the writer's legacy and foster educational, scientific, and cultural projects strengthening cooperation between Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan. The initiative was supported by the Consul General of Kyrgyzstan in Almaty and the Kyrgyz diaspora.

item.title: Commission Formed to Locate Burial Site of Kyrgyz Hero Abdykadyr Orozbekov
item.description: An interdepartmental commission has been established in Kyrgyzstan to identify and research the suspected burial site of Abdykadyr Orozbekov, a Hero of the Kyrgyz Republic. The commission, led by the Deputy Minister of Culture, Information, Youth Policy, includes historians, archaeologists, and scientists. Findings are due by December 20.

item.title: Over 1.2 Tons of Precursor Chemicals Seized in Uzbekistan from Truck Traveling to Tajikistan
item.description: Uzbekistan border customs officials at the "Sariosiyo" checkpoint seized over 1.2 tons of acetic anhydride, a precursor chemical, from a Volvo truck traveling from Kazakhstan to Tajikistan. The substance was found in 47 containers not declared in the shipping documents. An investigation is underway.

item.title: Bishkek Thermal Power Plant Navigates Heating Season with Sufficient Coal Reserves
item.description: As of November 18, Bishkek Thermal Power Plant (TPP) held 250,708 tons of coal, a decrease of 8,917 tons since October 20. The plant is operating normally, generating 8.961 million kWh of electricity and 8.4 thousand Gcal of heat daily. Total coal needed for the 2026-2027 season is estimated at 1.52 million tons.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Namangan Region Aims for $5.4 Billion in Foreign Investment by 2026
item.description: The Namangan region in Uzbekistan plans to attract $5.4 billion in foreign investment and achieve $1.2 billion in exports by the end of 2026. Further growth is projected for 2027, with targets of $7-8 billion in foreign investment and $1.3 billion in exports. New investment proposals totaling $5.4 billion have been prepared to meet these goals.

item.title: Illegal Works on Karatal River in Zhetysu Threatened Flooding, Water Inspection Intervenes
item.description: The Water Inspection has stopped illegal alteration of the Karatal River's course in the Zhetysu region, which could have led to bank erosion and flooding. Violators were fined. The works were conducted without the necessary state authority consent, disrupting the natural hydrological regime.

item.title: Uzbekistan: 1,500 Employees Dismissed in Anti-Corruption Drive Since Early 2026
item.description: Since the beginning of 2026, Uzbekistan has dismissed 1,500 employees as part of anti-corruption measures. Over 10 months, 5,368 internal investigations were conducted in state organizations. Additionally, violations related to conflicts of interest and affiliations totaling 297.4 billion soums were identified in public procurement.

item.title: Tajik Citizen Found Guilty in US of Funding ISIS, Faces Up to 55 Years
item.description: A federal jury in Brooklyn convicted a Tajik citizen, Manuchehr Mansouri, on four counts, including conspiracy to provide material support to ISIS and ISIS-Khorasan. The US Department of Justice reported he also faces charges for illegal firearm possession and providing false information to federal agents. He could receive up to 55 years in prison.

item.title: Ukrainian Drone Strikes Halve Russia's Oil Refining Volume in One Month
item.description: Ukrainian drone attacks have reduced crude oil refining at Russian refineries by approximately 45% since late October, according to two industry sources cited by Reuters. The attacks have disrupted or halted operations at 15 of Russia's 35 largest refineries, leading to a significant drop in daily processing volumes and impacting domestic fuel supply and exports.

item.title: Armenian PM Pashinyan Pledges Resignation After Peace Deal, Cites NATO Stance
item.description: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan stated his readiness to resign after signing a peace agreement with Azerbaijan, or if a new constitution is not approved by referendum. He proposed a referendum on the new constitution, suggesting he would step down in either scenario. Pashinyan also mentioned the 'Trump Route' and border delimitation as key steps in the peace process.

item.title: Uzbek Citizen Sentenced to 16 Months in South Korea for Funding Terror Group
item.description: A court in Seoul has sentenced a citizen of Uzbekistan to 16 months in prison for sending funds to a terror group in Syria. The individual was found guilty of violating anti-terrorism laws and ordered to pay a fine. The funds were transferred between January 2024 and January 2025.

item.title: Tanker Truck Overturns and Catches Fire in Shymkent, Driver Dies
item.description: A tanker truck overturned and caught fire in Shymkent following a road accident on the Tashkent highway. Rescuers found the body of a deceased man inside the vehicle's cabin. The fire, which spread to the spilled fuel, was extinguished over an area of 60 square meters.

item.title: Trump, Putin, and Xi to meet at APEC summit in China for first trilateral talks
item.description: US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and Chinese President Xi Jinping will hold their first trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, China, on November 19. The leaders are expected to discuss international security, nuclear disarmament, and global conflicts on the sidelines of the APEC summit.

item.title: Uzbekistan prioritizes economic potential in Namangan region with new investment projects
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev chaired a meeting focused on boosting reforms, attracting foreign investment, and increasing employment in the Namangan region. The region has significant potential for development through high technology, modern industry, and services, with projected foreign investment reaching $5.4 billion this year.

item.title: Astana to demolish residential building and political party office for LRT construction
item.description: Astana plans to demolish a 1950s residential building and the 'Adilet' party office to make way for the second phase of the light rail transit (LRT) project. The new lines will connect the left bank of the capital with the old railway station, requiring the expropriation of several properties.

item.title: CIS Interparliamentary Assembly Commission Meets in Turkmenistan's Avaza Resort
item.description: Delegations from Azerbaijan, Russia, and Belarus have arrived in Turkmenistan for a meeting of the CIS Interparliamentary Assembly's commission on political issues and international cooperation. The meeting, held in the Avaza resort zone, will discuss Turkmenistan's request for observer status within the CIS IPA.

item.title: Uzbekistan Accelerates New Tashkent Construction and Greening Projects
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev chaired a meeting on accelerating the construction of New Tashkent and the 'Yashil Makon' greening project. New incentives for investors were introduced. The focus is on new approaches, strict discipline, and daily monitoring of investment projects to create favorable conditions and remove obstacles.

item.title: UNICEF Reports 64 Children Killed and 64 Injured in Yemen Amid Escalating Conflict
item.description: UNICEF stated that at least 64 children have been killed and 64 injured in Yemen due to escalating conflict since September 3. The organization warned of further casualties as fighting continues in populated areas and essential services are affected. UNICEF is expanding its emergency response to assist up to 350,000 people.

item.title: OSCE Conference in Ashgabat Focuses on Peace and Parliamentary Diplomacy
item.description: The third Ashgabat Conference, 'The Role of Parliaments in Promoting International Law for Dialogue, Trust, and Security in the OSCE Space,' is underway in Ashgabat. Uzbekistan's delegation, led by the Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Chamber, is participating. The event is organized by the Mejlis of Turkmenistan and the OSCE.

item.title: Uzbekistan Showcases Mining Potential at COP31 Amid Climate Change Concerns
item.description: Uzbekistan is participating in the 31st session of the UN Climate Change Convention (COP31) in Antalya, Turkey, to discuss rational resource use, environmental balance, and industrial adaptation to climate change. The country aims to enhance international cooperation, adopt best practices, and attract investments in its mining sector.

item.title: Three Power Centers Influenced Kazakhstan's National Security Chief's Dismissal
item.description: The recent dismissal of Yermek Sagimbayev as head of Kazakhstan's National Security Committee (KNB) has sparked considerable media and public discussion. While some suggest personal reasons for his departure, sources indicate that Deputy Secretary of the Security Council Aida Balayeva, a group of KNB generals, and figures from the presidential administration influenced the decision.

item.title: Uzbekistan Convicts Four Judges for Unjust Decision in Assault Case
item.description: A district court in Uzbekistan has convicted four former appeals court judges for making an "unjust decision" by reducing a man's sentence in a high-profile assault and fraud case. Prosecutors argued corruption, while the defense claimed the trial undermined judicial independence and reforms.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Afghanistan to Increase Train Traffic on Hairatan-Mazar-i-Sharif Line
item.description: Uzbekistan and Afghanistan have agreed to increase train traffic on the Hairatan-Mazar-i-Sharif railway line. Officials discussed expanding cooperation in the railway sector and noted a significant increase in mutual cargo transportation this year. Both sides will take measures to effectively utilize existing opportunities.
